family.shared_definition: an absorbent piece of fabric used for wiping and drying surfaces or the body
family.neutral_stem: After spilling water on the counter, he grabbed
family.semantic_notes: Towel emphasizes looped or pile absorbent fabric meant for drying, while cloth is a generic term for any textile wiping rag.

source_context_dev: The bathroom sink had overflowed minutes earlier during a hurried morning routine. A heavy pile of soaked laundry sat right by the edge of the vanity.
He had just finished mopping up a large puddle near the shower basin. The sopping terry material was still dripping on the rack nearby.
The kids had tracked pool water across the entire master bathroom tile. Several thoroughly soaked items had been left in a sodden heap near the washbasin.
Someone had repeatedly rinsed their face without wringing out any of the thick terry items on the hook. Moisture was already pooling underneath them.

The utility drawer contained discarded scraps cut from old linens that had unraveled over years of hard scrubbing. Loose strands hung from their frayed borders.
A stack of tattered salvage materials sat beside the paint station. The edges were completely worn through from repeated harsh laundering.

The contexts bias bathroom/terry/heavy water scenarios for towel/wet versus workshop/rag-bin/aged-edge scenarios for cloth/frayed without mentioning any taboo lexical items.
